principles: Say what is true, not why you ask. A line earns its place only when it changes what the person does next; the age question, the birthday field and the download card stand without a justification. Benchmark: Apple HIG Writing (verified from Apple's documentation JSON, 15 Oct 2026): "Be clear. Choose words that are easily understood and convey the right thing. Check each word to be sure it needs to be there. If you can use fewer words, do so."

No "we" outside the three sanctioned promises (We never rewrite your words; the trust promise; We never imitate your voice). Mechanics, hints, errors, help and status lines say what happened with no speaker: "An um or an uh, taken out." not "You said um or uh. We took it out." Benchmark: Apple HIG Writing (verified): "Avoid using we altogether because it may be unclear who the 'we' in question refers to. This is particularly problematic in error messages like 'We're having trouble loading this content.' Something like 'Unable to load content' is much clearer."

Teach in context, once, where the thing happens. First run states three facts (what Word for word does, the voice is kept, private by default); how fixes work, that a name can be misheard, and the one-time download are explained at the first Review and in Settings, never twice. Benchmark: Apple HIG Onboarding (verified): "Consider providing a collection of context-specific tips instead of a single onboarding flow"; "design a brief, enjoyable experience that doesn't require people to memorize a lot of information"; "Don't let large downloads hinder onboarding."

Buttons are verbs with the outcome in them, 22 characters or fewer, never Yes, No or OK; the safe choice is the default and the destructive one is quiet. Benchmark: Apple HIG Alerts (verified): "Create succinct, logical button titles. Aim for a one- or two-word title that describes the result of selecting the button. Prefer verbs and verb phrases... avoiding 'Yes' and 'No'"; "If there's a destructive action, include a Cancel button to give people a clear, safe way to avoid the action."

A state screen names the state, keeps the words safe in one sentence, and offers one way forward; a loading screen says what is happening and, after eight seconds, that it is still happening. Benchmark: Apple HIG Alerts (verified): "Write a title that clearly and succinctly describes the situation... Avoid writing a title that doesn't convey useful information, like 'Error'"; Apple HIG Loading (verified): "Clearly communicate that content is loading and how long it might take to complete."

One name per thing, everywhere: letter (never entry), the book and {child}'s book, Month N (never chapter), small fix (never tidy, correction, edit), Word for word only in the promise and Settings, Exactly as said only when final equals raw, Read together, Plus with Plus Monthly and Plus Annual, this phone (never your phone), message (never note) for anything the app sends. Source: BRAND.md glossary, D-074, D-077, D-086. Benchmark: Day One keeps one vocabulary (entries, journals, On This Day) across app, site and export (memory, unverified).

One promise per screen, never repeated. trust.short appears once on Settings (the footer), the privacy line once in first run, and no privacy line on a screen where nobody is wondering; saying it twice sounds anxious. Source: VOICE.md "How we talk about privacy" (D-061). Benchmark: Apple Journal states privacy once, inside the feature it protects (BENCHMARK.md S5, read by the repo's benchmark; not fetched by me, unverified).

US English, because the app ships in the US storefront only (D-087, LEGAL-REQ-058): license, period, canceled, cellular data, right away, favorite, Mommy; prompts.ts already uses favorite, so the rest of the copy follows. Benchmark: Apple's own iOS strings ("Cellular", "License Agreement", "Recently Deleted") set the reference for a US launch (memory, unverified).

screens.screen: Age question (the first screen anyone sees)
screens.problem: "We ask everyone the same question." explains the ask with a "we" and reads as a disclaimer a bot adds to cover itself; nobody in the category justifies an age question. Yes and No pills plus a separate Continue turn one decision into three taps, and the disabled Continue sits a full screen away from the choice. The first impression is a bare form with no brand presence on warm paper.
screens.proposal: Delete ageGate.body (no replacement line; the question stands alone). Keep ageGate.title "Are you 18 or older?" exactly. Replace the radio pills and Continue with two equal, stacked 56 pt buttons that commit on tap: ageGate.yesButton "I am 18 or older" (16) and ageGate.noButton "I am under 18" (13); remove the Continue button from this screen. Fallback if counsel wants K-07's literal Yes and No: keep "Yes" and "No", drop the body line, and make the pills commit on tap. Visual: the quote-pair symbol (registry logo.symbol.accent, new context app.gate) at 24 pt above the question, the question in the hero serif, nothing else; no gradient or illustration before the welcome.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Writing (verified, Apple documentation JSON, 15 Oct 2026): "Avoid using we altogether because it may be unclear who the 'we' in question refers to" and "Check each word to be sure it needs to be there." Apple HIG Alerts (verified): "Create succinct, logical button titles... avoiding 'Yes' and 'No'." Regulated-brand age gates (one question, two buttons, no justification line) from memory, unverified.
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: The journey record cites A-REQ-030, which in docs/prd/A-entry-and-auth.md is "Offline entry"; the real requirements are PRD-REQ-019 (PRD.md K-07, founder 2 Oct 2026) and LEGAL-REQ-002 (P0) in docs/legal/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md, from CR-004 (Texas SB 2420 in force; Apple Declared Age Range). LEGAL-REQ-002 requires: the age question first on any first action, nothing preselected, an under-18 stop screen, a 24-hour closed gate, only the gate state stored. The proposal keeps all five: tap-to-commit means nothing is preselected, the question wording is unchanged, the stop screen and 24-hour rule are untouched, nothing new is stored. K-07's decision names "Yes and No" as the answers; that is product wording, not a statutory term, so the labelled buttons need a counsel nod, with the Yes/No fallback ready.

screens.problem: "Thank you for telling us." is a we-preamble in disguise; "Nothing you entered has been kept." reassures about nothing (the person entered one tap). Three lines do one job.
screens.proposal: ageGate.stopTitle becomes "{app} is currently for adults 18 and over." (the K-07 sentence as the serif title). Delete ageGate.stopBody. ageGate.stopNote becomes "Nothing was saved." Keep ageGate.mistakeButton "I answered by mistake" (21), shown only after 24 hours as now.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Alerts (verified): "Write a title that clearly and succinctly describes the situation"; "Include informative text only if it adds value."
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: K-07 and LEGAL-REQ-002 require a stop screen explaining the app is currently for adults 18 and over and that nothing but the gate state is stored; both facts stay. Only the time of the No is kept (D-026), so counsel may prefer "Nothing else was saved."
